name: Critical Thinking
alternateName: Critical Thinking: A Practical Guide to Seeing Through Bias, Noise and Manipulation
headline: A Practical Guide to Seeing Through Bias, Noise, and Manipulation

author.name: David G. Smith
author.jobTitle: Data Scientist, Technical Architect & Strategic Advisor
author.description: Engineer, technical architect, and author specializing in federal technology modernization, cloud architecture, and applied cognitive decision-making models.

publisher.name: David G. Smith Publishing
publisher.description: Independent publisher of non-fiction works focusing on critical thinking and technology.

description: An exhaustive, high-depth 466-page practical manual synthesizing cognitive psychology, formal logic, statistical risk assessment, and decision-making frameworks. Designed to help professionals, analysts, and readers identify cognitive biases, navigate digital manipulation, survive AI chatbot sycophancy, and implement robust metacognitive controls.
educationalUse: Self-Paced Professional Training & Applied Logic Curriculum

about.name: Cognitive Bias Mitigation
about.description: Protocols for identifying and correcting System 1 intuition errors, narrative fallacies, and the Bias Blind Spot (Emily Pronin).

about.name: Statistical Risk Literacy
about.description: Evaluating absolute vs. relative risk, base rates, and Bayesian updating based on Gerd Gigerenzer's risk models.

about.name: AI Chatbot Sycophancy & Digital Defenses
about.description: Tactical frameworks (including the AI Crux Test) for identifying algorithmic echo chambers, digital dark patterns, and automated confirmation bias.

about.name: Strategic Decision Frameworks
about.description: Operationalizing Gary Klein's Premortem, Colonel John Boyd's OODA Loop, Second-Order Thinking, and Red Team Thinking.

about.name: Constructive Disagreement Models
about.description: Interpersonal truth-seeking tools including Steelmanning, the Ideological Turing Test, and Double Crux alignment.

hasPart.name: Part I: The Flawed Machine
hasPart.description: Deconstructs evolutionary hardware bugs, narrative fallacies, and the neurobiology of emotion (Somatic Marker Hypothesis).

hasPart.name: Part II: The Mechanics of Thinking
hasPart.description: Formalizes deductive, inductive, and abductive proof structures alongside statistical self-defense and risk dynamics.

hasPart.name: Part III: Information in the Wild
hasPart.description: Navigates descriptive vs. normative claims, lateral reading, CRAAP test vetting, dark patterns, and AI chatbot sycophancy.

hasPart.name: Part IV: The Advanced Toolkit
hasPart.description: Operational models covering second-order systems, Bayesian updating, productive disagreement, and metacognitive calibration.

differentiators.scientificVetting: Fully post-replication-crisis vetted, excluding failed social priming and un-replicated behavioral experiments.
differentiators.aiScope: Dedicated chapter (Chapter 11) on surviving conversational AI chatbot sycophancy and digital dark patterns.
differentiators.practicalExercises: Includes chapter-ending practical worksheets including the Personal Bias Inventory (PBI) and 5-Minute Friday Audit.
